CAA Successful Prosecutions
1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025




                                                       OFFICIAL - Public

                                OFFICIAL - Public. This information has been cleared for unrestricted distribution.
1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025                                                                                         CAA Successful Prosecutions




      Defendant
      Barry SCOTT

      Brief Description
      Barry Scott was the pilot in command of Piper PA-28 aircraft on an evening flight from
      Blackbushe to Dunkeswell and back. A passenger, who was a private pilot, accompanied
      Mr Scott on the flight. The outward flight took-off later than planned and took longer than
      planned to reach Dunkeswell. The return flight took-off after sunset. Blackbushe was not
      operational after 1800 so there was no RFFS, no lighting and no flight information service.
      The aircraft was off track as it approached Blackbushe. The passenger suggested
      diverting to Farnborough but Mr Scott pressed-on. Mr Scott descended the aircraft to 800
      feet a.g.l in the Sandhurst area, as if approaching to land, causing the passenger to shout
      that it was not Blackbushe. The passenger could see National Grid power cables so close
      to the aircraft that it would have struck them had the undercarriage been down. A local
      resident, also a pilot, saw the aircraft fly very low over their house, assumed it was in
      trouble and prepared to call the emergency services. The passenger told Mr Scott to
      declare a PAN and to go to Farnborough but Mr Scott continued to fly orbits. Ambient
      lighting from nearby premises identified Blackbushe; the runway was barely visible. The
      aircraft landed.

      Mr Scott pleaded guilty to negligently endangering an aircraft.

      Date
      28/05/2024

      Court
      Reading Crown Court

      Sentence
      Fine £1,500



      Defendant
      Charles HUDSON

      Brief Description
      Mr Hudson was the pilot in command of a Folland Gnat aircraft on a flight from/to North
      Weald. He flew within the Stansted TMZ without operating the aircraft's transponder. He
      then flew twice within class D controlled airspace, the Stansted CTR, without air traffic
      control clearance, causing loss of separation with a passenger flight inbound to Stansted.
      A second inbound aircraft was given avoiding action and broken-off from final approach. A
      third inbound flight had to be instructed to turn away from final approach and climb, and a
      fourth inbound aircraft was instructed to orbit and turned away from final approach. As Mr


                                                                OFFICIAL - Public

                                OFFICIAL - Public. This information has been cleared for unrestricted distribution.
1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025                                                                                         CAA Successful Prosecutions




      Hudson approached North Weald, he flew over the village of North Weald Bassett at
      between 525 and 541 feet a.g.l.

      Mr Hudson pleaded guilty to flying within a TMZ without operating a transponder, two
      offences of flying within class D airspace without air traffic control clearance and one
      offence of flying over a congested area at a height less than 1,000 feet.

      Date
      29/08/2024

      Court
      Chelmsford Magistrates' Court

      Sentence
      Fine £4,000



      Defendant
      Gordon OLIVER

      Brief Description
      Gordon Oliver organised the annual Buttermere Bash event. Previously, permission for a
      flying display at the event had been applied for and granted by the CAA. In 2024 however,
      Mr Oliver deliberately did not apply to the CAA for permission and flying displays took
      place.

      Mr Oliver pleaded guilty to organising a flying display without having applied for and
      obtained CAA permission.

      Date
      09/01/2025

      Court
      Carlisle Magistrates' Court

      Sentence
      Fine £1,675

1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025                                                                                         CAA Successful Prosecutions




      Defendant
      David HOARE

      Brief Description
      David Hoare was the pilot of a paramotor aircraft which flew at less than 500 feet at West
      Bay beach, Bridport.

      Mr Hoare was convicted of one offence of low flying.

      Date

      18/02/2025

      Court

      Weymouth Magistrates' Court

      Sentence
      Fine £1,500



      Defendant
      Simon NICHOLLS

      Brief Description
      Simon Nicholls was the pilot of a Robinson R44 helicopter which flew over congested
      areas of Worksop.

      Mr Nicholls pleaded guilty to two offences of low flying over congested areas.

      Date

      06/03/2025

      Court

      Mansfield Magistrates' Court

      Sentence
      Fine £1,280

1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025                                                                                         CAA Successful Prosecutions




      Defendant
      Christopher HOLLANDS

      Brief Description
      Christopher Hollands was the pilot in command and pilot monitoring a commercial airline
      flight from Oslo to Manchester. Mr Hollands did not make radio contact with air traffic
      control as the flight entered UK airspace and for more than 30 minutes thereafter did not
      hear repeated radio calls from ATC, other aircraft and the Distress and Diversion cell,
      causing a security incident. Two RAF Typhoons were launched, intercepted the aircraft
      and escorted it into Manchester airport, where police attended.

      Mr Hollands pleaded guilty to not maintaining continuous air-ground communication watch
      and establishing two-way communication with the appropriate air traffic control units.

      Date
      20/03/2025

      Court
      Manchester Magistrates' Court

      Sentence
      Fine £4,511
